references.text: The psalmist speaks to the foolish (ἄφρονες) and asks whether he who planted the ear does not hear, and whether he who formed the eye does not see. The same logic as in Luke 11:40: He who created the outer also created the inner. [ref:Ps 94:8-9|Psalms 94:8-9]

God created humanity – both the outer (the body) and the inner (in His image). Jesus' argument presupposes that God is the Creator of the whole person, which is grounded in the creation account. [ref:Gen 1:26-27|Genesis 1:26-27]

Isaiah warns those who try to hide their plans from the Lord in the depths and asks: "Shall the clay say to him who forms it, 'He has not made me'?" The same reasoning: The Creator knows both the outer and the inner. [ref:Isa 29:15-16|Isaiah 29:15-16]

Jesus' parallel statement in Matthew: "Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! You clean the outside of the cup and the dish, but inside they are full of greed and self-indulgence. You blind Pharisee! First clean the inside of the cup, so that the outside may also become clean!" This is the parallel passage to Luke 11:39-40. [ref:Matt 23:25-26|Matthew 23:25-26]
The Lord does not look at the outer appearance but at the heart. God, who created the outer, also created the inner, and it is the inner that matters most to Him. [ref:1 Sam 16:7|1 Samuel 16:7]

Proverbs states that "the fear of the Lord is the beginning of knowledge; only fools (ἄφρονες in the LXX) despise wisdom and discipline." Jesus uses the same word – ἄφρονες – about the Pharisees who do not realize that the Creator of the outer also created the inner. [ref:Prov 1:7|Proverbs 1:7]

"I, the Lord, search the heart and test the mind." God, who formed humanity outwardly, also examines the inner being. The Pharisees' focus on external purity overlooks that God sees the inner person. [ref:Jer 17:10|Jeremiah 17:10]

"No creature is hidden from Him. All things are naked and exposed to the eyes of Him to whom we must give account." He who created the outer also knows the inner – nothing is hidden from the Creator. [ref:Heb 4:13|Hebrews 4:13]
